To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proteins of human tonsillar ribosomes are different in their electrophoretic mobility from the proteins of human placenta, rabbit reticulocyte and rat liver ribosomes.
“The proteins of human tonsillar 40-S and 60-S subunits were separated and identified by 2D gel electrophoresis and the results were compared with other mammalian cells”.
34 proteins were identified in 40-S ribosomal subunit of human tonsillar tissue. 35 proteins were identified in the 60-S ribosomal subunits of human tonsillary lymphatic tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the separation of the proteins of human tonsillar ribosomal subunits and the identification of these proteins by two-dimensional electrophoresis.
the separation of the ribosomal proteins in human tonsil by two-dimensional polyacylamide-gel-electrophoresis.
the separation of the proteins in cytoplasmic human ribosomal subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteins of human tonsillar ribosomes are very similar to those of the other eukaryotic ribosomes studied so far.
the 40-S and 60-S subunits of human tonsillar ribosomes contain 34 and 35 proteins respectively and that 65 proteins can be identified as different from one another.
the proteins of human ribosomal subunits have electrophoretic properties which are very similar to those of rat and rabbit ribosomal subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
34 proteins are associated with the small subunit, 35 with the large subunit, and 65 proteins are present in both subunits.
the proteins associated with human tonsillar ribosomes were found to be similar to the ribosomal proteins from other mammalian sources.
40 proteins are common to the ribosomes of human tonsil and placenta, and 36 proteins are common to ribosomes of human placenta, rabbit reticulocyte, rat liver and human tonsil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 40S ribosome subunit has a higher protein content than the 60S subunit, which is consistent with previous studies.
the human ribosomal proteins can be identified and classified according to their mobility in two-dimensional electrophoresis.
the 60-S and 40-S subunits are composed of 35 and 34 proteins, respectively.
